title: The RCB Victory Parade Stampede
dek: Royal Challengers Bengaluru's first IPL title in 18 years turned deadly when an unpermitted victory celebration drew lakhs of fans to a Bengaluru stadium, killing 11 people. A judicial inquiry later found the team, its event partner, and police had all failed to plan for the crowd they knew was coming.

heroStat.label: people killed in the stampede outside M. Chinnaswamy Stadium on June 4, 2025

promise.quote: The victory celebration will be a safe, well-organised event for our fans.
promise.madeBy: Royal Challengers Bengaluru (RCB) and event partner DNA Entertainment Networks
promise.role: IPL franchise and its hired event management company
promise.context: Implicit assurance underlying the announcement of a public victory celebration in Bengaluru after RCB won its first IPL title, held the day after the final on June 3, 2025.

target.description: A public celebration conducted with prior permission from licensing authorities, adequate crowd-control planning, and coordination with police proportionate to the crowd size expected.
target.standard: Karnataka's Licensing and Controlling of Assemblies and Processions Order, 2009, which requires prior permission for large public gatherings.

reality.description: An estimated three to five lakh (300,000-500,000) people converged on and around M. Chinnaswamy Stadium on June 4, 2025, for a celebration held without the required prior permission from the licensing authority. A crush developed as the crowd surged, killing 11 people and injuring more than 50. A judicial commission led by Justice John Michael Cunha found RCB, KSCA, and DNA Entertainment Networks responsible for organising a gathering of that scale without permission, and flagged lapses by police officers, including the then Bengaluru police commissioner, who was subsequently suspended. A Central Administrative Tribunal separately held RCB accountable.

gap.metricLabel: Crowd size the organisers had permission for vs. the crowd that actually turned out
gap.targetDisplay: No prior permission was obtained for any public assembly of this scale
gap.actualDisplay: ~3-5 lakh people estimated to have gathered
gap.note: The 400,000 actual figure is the midpoint of the three-to-five-lakh range cited by the Central Administrative Tribunal; there was no permitted crowd size because no permission was sought.

timeline.label: RCB wins IPL 2025 title
timeline.detail: Royal Challengers Bengaluru wins its first IPL championship, prompting plans for a victory celebration.

timeline.label: Stampede at Chinnaswamy Stadium
timeline.detail: A crush develops outside the stadium amid an unpermitted crowd estimated at three to five lakh people, killing 11 and injuring more than 50.

timeline.label: Police probe intensifies
timeline.detail: Karnataka Police intensify their investigation; the state government orders CID to take over the probe.

timeline.label: Justice Cunha commission report submitted
timeline.detail: The judicial inquiry led by Justice John Michael Cunha submits a two-volume report to Chief Minister Siddaramaiah, recommending legal action against RCB, KSCA, DNA Entertainment Networks, and suspended police officers.

legalStatus.summary: This is a stub entry. A judicial commission has recommended legal action against RCB, KSCA, the event management company, and specific suspended police officers; this entry has not yet traced whether formal criminal charges have been filed or concluded against any of them.

verdict.summary: Preliminary verdict, pending fuller research: the judicial inquiry's finding that the celebration was held without required permission, at a scale organisers should reasonably have anticipated, is well documented; what remains unresolved is whether any of the parties found responsible have faced concrete legal consequences.
verdict.reasoning: The core facts — death toll, absence of permission, and the Cunha commission's findings — are corroborated across multiple independent outlets. The eventual legal outcome for RCB, KSCA, and individual officials was still pending as of this entry's research.

incomplete: Whether RCB, KSCA, or DNA Entertainment Networks have faced formal criminal charges or penalties following the Cunha commission's recommendations has not been established here.
The individual identities and final departmental outcomes for the suspended police officers, including the former commissioner, have not been fully detailed in this entry.
Compensation paid to victims' families, if any, has not been tracked here.
